What you will learn

01 / DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING

From a problem to a policy

State representations, the principle of optimality, finite and infinite horizons, value iteration and policy iteration.

02 / REINFORCEMENT LEARNING

Learning through interaction

Exploration, Monte Carlo methods, temporal-difference learning, Q-learning and function approximation.

03 / METHODS & APPLICATIONS

Connecting theory and practice

Policy gradients, sequential decision experiments, and reinforcement learning for language models.

The lecture outline is a proposed plan; final sequencing may change.

About the course

This course introduces the basic models and solution methods of dynamic programming and reinforcement learning. We connect mathematical ideas to modeling, algorithm design and experiments on sequential decision problems.

Preparation

Basic probability, linear algebra and optimization, plus programming experience. Python will be useful for the proposed computational exercises.

Learning outcomes

  • Formulate a sequential decision problem and identify its assumptions.
  • Derive and implement core planning and learning algorithms.
  • Evaluate policies and explain computational and statistical tradeoffs.

Grading, assignment deadlines and office hours: to be announced.
